title: Kernelized synthetic load harness to surface p95/p99 drift across endpoint-model-region slices
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a synthetic traffic harness and dashboarding layer that computes tokens/sec and tail quantiles (p95, p99) sliced by endpoint, model variant, and region. The harness will run controlled traffic shapes (steady, burst, long-tail) and seed representative KV/prefix cache states to create repeatable baselines. Outputs feed a compact dashboard and automated regression detector that surfaces statistically significant drift versus rolling baselines.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Public dashboard surfaceable in Console with dropdowns for endpoint, model, and region and timepicker; 2) Metrics emitted: tokens.processed/sec, latency.p95.ms, latency.p99.ms, request.count; 3) Synthetic harness can run three traffic profiles and reproduce baseline within ±5% for tokens/sec; 4) Regression detector creates alerts when p95 or p99 deviates beyond configured thresholds with attached sample traces and cost delta estimate; 5) Backfill + historical compare runs for at least 14 days of telemetry.
technical_notes: Metric names follow existing telemetry conventions: latency.pXX.ms (aggregated using nearest-quantile algorithm in telemetry pipeline), tokens.processed/sec (rate counter), route and model encoded as tags: route_name, model_id, region. We will add a lightweight slice key: slice = route_name|model_id|region to accelerate rollups. Use streaming aggregator to emit both windowed quantiles (60s, 5m, 1h) and daily rollups. Storage retention for high-cardinality slices limited to 30 days at 1m resolution to control cost.
implementation_plan: 1) Instrument synthetic harness runner (Go) to parameterize sequences (length distribution, temperature, batch size) and cache priming sets. 2) Hook harness output to telemetry pipeline via existing metrics exporter (PR: github.com/redwood/infer/PR-5678). 3) Add slice-key producer to telemetry SDK and incremental rollup stage. 4) Build Console panels: time-series p95/p99, tokens/sec heatmap, and a compact slice explorer that paginates top-200 slices by QPS. 5) Implement regression detector: bootstrap CI + changepoint detector for abrupt shifts; Mann-Whitney for gradual drift. 6) Add alert templates and a “rerun harness” button on the slice detail page.
test_plan: Unit tests for exporter and slice-key logic + e2e run in staging with 3 canonical traffic profiles. Validation checks: 1) Reproducibility: baseline run on staging twice with <5% variability; 2) Noise injection: simulate a 20% kernel slowdown and assert detector fires within configured window; 3) Dashboards render for 50k unique slices without UI timeouts (pagination test). Load tests use dedicated small cluster (dedicated-dev) to avoid affecting prod telemetry.
roll_out_plan: Stage 1: feature-flagged deployment to staging and internal Canary org. Stage 2: opt-in beta for several internal teams (SRE, Platform, Search). Stage 3: gradual enable for all orgs with default retention limits. Communicate breaking changes (new slice key tag) in DevX notes and provide migration guidance.
notes_and_tradeoffs: - To control cardinality we avoid storing raw slice-series at 1s resolution; choose 1m for high-card slices. - Statistical tests trade sensitivity vs false positives; bootstrap CI gives robust effect sizes but costs compute. We'll cap detector runs to top-200 slices by QPS and provide an async backfill for lower-QPS slices. - Priming cache state is synthetic; may not fully reflect customer production cache distributions; document limitations in dashboard.
